business_problem: Vodafone Ireland needed to modernize its TOBi virtual assistant because an older assistant deployment could no longer meet containment goals or take advantage of the newer generative-AI, NLU, and self-learning capabilities available in the latest platform.
solution_summary: Vodafone Ireland worked with IBM Technology Expert Labs to redeploy its TOBi virtual assistant on the latest IBM watsonx Assistant release. The modernization introduced generative-AI features that use retrieval-augmented generation against Vodafone content so the assistant can provide grounded, conversational answers instead of relying only on legacy dialog design. The new platform also includes a transformer-based natural-language-understanding engine that classifies requests with less training effort, plus self-learning algorithms that improve routing and response quality from prior interactions. During the migration, Vodafone comprehensively rebuilt TOBi's conversational journeys and adjusted its surrounding application infrastructure so the assistant could exploit the upgraded NLU and RAG stack. The result is a more maintainable customer-service architecture that lets teams create new journeys faster while improving containment and reducing misunderstood utterances.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx Assistant

data_flow: Customer messages enter TOBi, watsonx Assistant retrieves grounded content from Vodafone sources with RAG, its NLU model classifies the request and routes the conversation, and the self-learning mechanisms use prior interactions to improve future responses and journey handling.
business_outcome: Vodafone Ireland improved customer-assistant containment, reduced misinterpretation of user requests, and accelerated the creation of new conversational journeys after redeploying TOBi on the latest assistant platform.
